candidates.sentence: She will vote against Mitch McConnell’s and far-right Republicans’ national abortion ban.
She successfully repealed a painful 40% tax on many middle class Nevadans’ health plans, a promise from her 2016 Senate campaign.

Catherine has been a fierce leader in the fight for reproductive freedom, earning a 100% score in National Abortion Rights Action League’s (NARAL) Congressional Record on Choice every year she has served in the Senate.

She has helped lead the Women’s Health Protection Act, which would enshrine Roe protections into federal law and guarantee equal access to abortion in every corner of the nation, and she has championed legislation to protect a woman’s right to travel to a different state to access the care they need.

She stood strong for Nevada’s mining industry, single-handedly stopping new mining taxes which would have hurt a critical rural industry and the tens of thousands of good-paying Nevada jobs it supports.
When the coronavirus hit, she helped to cut the cost of health care coverage by an average of $444 per month and helped over 40,000 Nevadans become eligible for coverage.
Catherine knows the student loan system is broken and has fought to protect student borrowers, improve access to student loans, and allow students to refinance their loan debt at lower rates.
Catherine has been a champion for renewable energy, leading the fight for a solar tax credit that helps tackle climate change and create Nevada jobs.
That’s why she’s proud to stand with Dreamers and continue to fight for comprehensive immigration reform — including a pathway to citizenship.
She was the deciding vote to pass about $3,000 in middle-class tax cuts to Nevada families because she knows Nevadans deserve to keep more of the money they earn.
